--- title: "Data & methods" subtitle: "How the data were collected, combined, analysed, and published" --- ## The pipeline at a glance ```{mermaid} flowchart LR A["DHS surveys
children & households
(IPUMS-DHS)"] --> C["1 · Cluster table
anemia %, open defecation %,
wealth, education"] B["DHS GPS
cluster locations"] --> C C --> D["2 · Buffers
2 km urban / 5 km rural"] E["Malaria Atlas Project
PfPR raster, 2000–2021
(web API)"] --> F["Zonal statistics
rasterio + rasterstats"] G["CHIRPS monthly rainfall
1981–2021
(xarray)"] --> F D --> F H["geoBoundaries
admin-1 regions
(web API)"] --> K F --> I["4 · k-means profiles
+ DBSCAN hotspots"] F --> J["5 · Random forest vs
linear regression"] I --> K["6 · Aggregate to hexagons
& regions (privacy)"] J --> K K --> L["Quarto website
folium + Altair"] ``` ## Data sources | Source | What it gives | How it was collected | Years | |---|---|---|---| | **DHS surveys** via IPUMS-DHS | Children's hemoglobin (anemia), household toilet type, wealth quintile, mother's education, interview date | Registered download (restricted, *not* in this repo) | 2000–2021 | | **DHS GPS files** | Displaced cluster coordinates (up to 2 km urban, 5 km rural, rarely 10 km) | Registered download (restricted) | 2000–2021 | | **Malaria Atlas Project** | *P. falciparum* parasite rate in children 2–10, 5 km raster, one per year | **Web Coverage Service API** (`GetCoverage`, clipped to Africa) | 2000–2021 | | **CHIRPS v2** | Monthly rainfall, 0.05° (~5 km) raster | Monthly netCDF files | 1981–2021 | | **geoBoundaries** | Admin-1 (province/state) boundaries | **geoBoundaries REST API**, one call per country | current | ::: {#a063b800 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html} Sample: from 3 million child records to the analysis sample
Step Children remaining
All child records 3,015,819
Sub-Saharan Africa 1,475,438
Child alive 1,363,997
Aged 6-59 months 751,676
Tested for anemia 319,126
Cluster has GPS coordinates 284,974

Children in clusters with >= 5 tested children 236,822
``` ::: ::: The final sample has **236\,822 children** in **22\,097 clusters** across **28 countries** and **68 surveys**. Clusters with fewer than 5 tested children were dropped because their anemia rate is too noisy. ## Step 1 · From children to clusters A DHS **cluster** is a village or urban neighbourhood where about 25–30 households were interviewed. For each cluster I calculate: - **Anemia (%)**: the share of tested children aged 6–59 months with hemoglobin below 11 g/dL (adjusted for altitude by DHS) - **Open defecation (%)**: the share of households with no toilet facility - **Wealth**: the average household wealth quintile (1 = poorest fifth of the country, 5 = richest) - **Mothers with secondary school (%)**, **urban/rural**, and the **interview month** ::: {.callout-note collapse=true} ## Show the code: `analysis/01_build_clusters.py` (pandas) ```python """Step 1. Turn DHS child records into one row per survey cluster. Input : IPUMS-DHS extract (private) Output: data/private/clusters.parquet (private: contains GPS) """ import numpy as np import pandas as pd import pyreadstat from config import DHS_FILE, PRIVATE, SSA, MIN_CHILDREN cols = ["sample", "country", "year", "idhspsu", "intyear", "monthint", "urban", "wealthq", "educlvl", "kidalive", "kidagemo", "anemialvlkid", "opentoiletpsu", "gpslat", "gpslong", "perweight"] print("Reading DHS extract (this takes a few minutes)...") d, meta = pyreadstat.read_dta(str(DHS_FILE), usecols=cols) print(f" {len(d):,} child records, {d.country.nunique()} countries") flow = [("All child records", len(d))] def keep(mask, label): global d d = d[mask] flow.append((label, len(d))) keep(d.country.isin(SSA.keys()), "Sub-Saharan Africa") keep(d.kidalive == 1, "Child alive") keep(d.kidagemo.between(6, 59), "Aged 6-59 months") keep(d.anemialvlkid.isin([1, 2, 3, 4]), "Tested for anemia") ok_gps = d.gpslat.notna() & d.gpslong.notna() & ~((d.gpslat == 0) & (d.gpslong == 0)) keep(ok_gps, "Cluster has GPS coordinates") keep(d.opentoiletpsu.between(0, 100), "Cluster open defecation share available") keep(d.urban.isin([1, 2]), "Urban/rural known") d["anemic"] = (d.anemialvlkid <= 3).astype(float) # any anemia (Hb < 11 g/dL, altitude-adjusted) d["mod_sev"] = (d.anemialvlkid <= 2).astype(float) # moderate or severe d["mom_secondary"] = np.where(d.educlvl.isin([0, 1, 2, 3]), (d.educlvl >= 2).astype(float), np.nan) d["country_name"] = d.country.map(SSA) d["wealthq_ok"] = d.wealthq.where(d.wealthq.between(1, 5)) g = d.groupby("idhspsu") cl = pd.DataFrame({ "sample": g["sample"].first(), "country": g["country_name"].first(), "survey_year": g["year"].first(), "int_year": g["intyear"].agg(lambda s: s.mode().iat[0]).astype(int), "int_month": g["monthint"].agg(lambda s: s.mode().iat[0]).astype(int), "urban": (g["urban"].first() == 1).astype(int), "lat": g["gpslat"].first(), "lon": g["gpslong"].first(), "n_children": g.size(), "anemia_pct": g["anemic"].mean() * 100, "modsev_anemia_pct": g["mod_sev"].mean() * 100, "od_pct": g["opentoiletpsu"].first(), "wealth": g["wealthq_ok"].mean(), # mean household wealth quintile, 1 = poorest, 5 = richest (relative to own country) "mom_secondary_pct": g["mom_secondary"].mean() * 100, }).reset_index() n_before = len(cl) cl = cl[cl.n_children >= MIN_CHILDREN].copy() flow.append((f"Children in clusters with >= {MIN_CHILDREN} tested children", int(cl.n_children.sum()))) cl.to_parquet(PRIVATE / "clusters.parquet", index=False) pd.DataFrame(flow, columns=["step", "remaining"]).to_csv(PRIVATE / "sample_flow.csv", index=False) print(pd.DataFrame(flow, columns=["step", "remaining"]).to_string(index=False)) print(f"Clusters: {n_before:,} -> {len(cl):,} kept; {cl.country.nunique()} countries; " f"{cl['sample'].nunique()} surveys; years {cl.int_year.min()}-{cl.int_year.max()}") print(cl.groupby("country").size().sort_values(ascending=False).to_string()) print(cl[["anemia_pct", "od_pct", "wealth", "mom_secondary_pct", "n_children"]].describe().round(2).to_string()) ``` ::: ## Step 2 · Raster analysis: malaria and rainfall around each cluster DHS moves every cluster's GPS point by up to 2 km (urban) or 5 km (rural) to protect privacy. So instead of reading the raster at the point, I draw a **buffer** of that size around each point (in an equal-area projection, so the distances are in true metres) and take the **mean raster value inside the buffer** with `rasterstats.zonal_stats`. - **Malaria:** the Malaria Atlas Project raster *for the year of the interview*, read with `rasterio`. - **Rainfall anomaly:** with `xarray`, I sum CHIRPS rainfall over the **3 months before the interview month**. I compare that total to the same 3 calendar months in every year from 1981 to 2010 at the same pixel: *z = (this year − 30-year average) / 30-year standard deviation*. Negative means drier than normal, positive means wetter. - **Typical annual rainfall:** the 1981–2010 average. As a check, the rainfall anomalies correlate at **0.78** with the ones computed independently in R from the daily CHIRPS v3 data in my other project. The two use different CHIRPS versions and different window definitions, so they should not match exactly. ::: {.callout-note collapse=true} ## Show the code: `analysis/02_raster_features.py` (geopandas, rasterio, rasterstats, xarray) ```python """Step 2. Add raster-based features to each cluster (zonal statistics). * Buffers: 2 km (urban) / 5 km (rural), matching DHS GPS displacement. * Malaria: Malaria Atlas Project P. falciparum prevalence (age 2-10), mean over the buffer, for the cluster's interview year. * Rainfall: CHIRPS monthly. Total rain in the 3 months before the interview month, as a standardized anomaly (z-score) against the same 3 calendar months in 1981-2010 at that location. Plus the long-term (1981-2010) mean annual rainfall. Input : data/private/clusters.parquet Output: data/private/clusters_features.parquet """ import numpy as np import pandas as pd import geopandas as gpd import rasterio import xarray as xr from rasterio.transform import from_origin from rasterstats import zonal_stats from config import PRIVATE, CHIRPS_MONTHLY, MAP_DIR, AFRICA_BBOX, AFRICA_EQUAL_AREA cl = pd.read_parquet(PRIVATE / "clusters.parquet") pts = gpd.GeoDataFrame(cl, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(cl.lon, cl.lat), crs="EPSG:4326") # ---- buffers (in metres, using an equal-area projection) ------------------ pts_m = pts.to_crs(AFRICA_EQUAL_AREA) radius = np.where(pts_m.urban == 1, 2000, 5000) buf = pts_m.buffer(radius).to_crs("EPSG:4326") print(f"{len(buf):,} buffers built") def zonal_mean(geoms, array, transform, nodata): out = zonal_stats(list(geoms), array, affine=transform, stats=["mean"], nodata=nodata, all_touched=True) return np.array([o["mean"] if o["mean"] is not None else np.nan for o in out]) # ---- malaria (MAP PfPR 2-10), matched to interview year -------------------- cl["pfpr"] = np.nan for yr, idx in cl.groupby(cl.int_year.clip(2000, 2021)).groups.items(): with rasterio.open(MAP_DIR / f"PfPR_2-10_Africa_{yr}.tif") as src: arr = src.read(1).astype("float32") nod = src.nodata if nod is not None: arr[arr == nod] = np.nan arr[arr < 0] = np.nan cl.loc[idx, "pfpr"] = zonal_mean(buf.loc[idx], arr, src.transform, np.nan) * 100 print(f" malaria {yr}: {len(idx):,} clusters") # ---- rainfall (CHIRPS monthly) -------------------------------------------- lon0, lat0, lon1, lat1 = AFRICA_BBOX YEARS = range(1981, 2022) BASE = (1981, 2010) def open_year(y): ds = xr.open_dataset(CHIRPS_MONTHLY / f"CHIRPS_monthly_{y}.nc") return ds["precip"].sel(longitude=slice(lon0, lon1), latitude=slice(lat1, lat0)) # load all years once (Africa subset), as a dict of (12, ny, nx) float32 arrays print("Loading CHIRPS (Africa subset)...") rain = {} for y in range(YEARS.start - 1, YEARS.stop): try: da = open_year(y) except FileNotFoundError: continue rain[y] = da.values.astype("float32") lats, lons = da.latitude.values, da.longitude.values res = abs(float(lons[1] - lons[0])) transform = from_origin(lons.min() - res / 2, lats.max() + res / 2, res, res) def three_month_total(y, end_month): """Rain total for the 3 months ending in end_month (1-12) of year y.""" tot = 0 for k in range(3): m, yy = end_month - k, y if m <= 0: m, yy = m + 12, y - 1 if yy not in rain: return None tot = tot + rain[yy][m - 1] return tot # long-term mean annual rainfall (1981-2010) annual = np.nanmean([rain[y].sum(axis=0) for y in range(BASE[0], BASE[1] + 1)], axis=0) cl["rain_annual_mm"] = zonal_mean(buf, annual, transform, np.nan) # 3-month anomaly: window ends the month BEFORE the interview month end = cl.int_month - 1 end_year = np.where(end == 0, cl.int_year - 1, cl.int_year) end = np.where(end == 0, 12, end) cl["rain_end_month"], cl["rain_end_year"] = end, end_year cl["rain_3mo_mm"] = np.nan cl["rain_3mo_z"] = np.nan for e in range(1, 13): base = [three_month_total(y, e) for y in range(BASE[0], BASE[1] + 1)] base = np.stack([b for b in base if b is not None]) # 1981 Jan/Feb windows need 1980 (no data) mu, sd = base.mean(axis=0), base.std(axis=0) sd[sd < 1] = np.nan # near-zero variability (desert) -> undefined for y in sorted(set(end_year[end == e])): idx = cl.index[(end == e) & (end_year == y)] tot = three_month_total(y, e) z = np.clip((tot - mu) / sd, -5, 5) cl.loc[idx, "rain_3mo_mm"] = zonal_mean(buf.loc[idx], tot, transform, np.nan) cl.loc[idx, "rain_3mo_z"] = zonal_mean(buf.loc[idx], z, transform, np.nan) print(f" rainfall window ending month {e:2d} done") cl.to_parquet(PRIVATE / "clusters_features.parquet", index=False) print(cl[["pfpr", "rain_annual_mm", "rain_3mo_mm", "rain_3mo_z"]].describe().round(2).to_string()) print("Missing:", cl[["pfpr", "rain_3mo_z"]].isna().sum().to_dict()) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse=true} ## Show the code: `analysis/03_download_boundaries.py` (geoBoundaries API) ```python """Step 3. Download admin-1 (region/province) boundaries from the geoBoundaries API. Source: geoBoundaries (www.geoboundaries.org), open licence, CC BY 4.0. Output: data/public/admin1.geojson (public data, safe to commit) """ import json import time import urllib.request import geopandas as gpd import pandas as pd from config import PUBLIC, PRIVATE, SSA, ISO3 name_to_code = {v: k for k, v in SSA.items()} countries = pd.read_parquet(PRIVATE / "clusters.parquet", columns=["country"]).country.unique() def get_json(url, tries=4): for i in range(tries): try: with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=120) as r: return json.loads(r.read()) except Exception as e: print(f" retry {i + 1}: {e}") time.sleep(2 ** i) raise RuntimeError(url) frames = [] for c in sorted(countries): iso = ISO3[name_to_code[c]] meta = get_json(f"https://www.geoboundaries.org/api/current/gbOpen/{iso}/ADM1/") g = gpd.read_file(meta["simplifiedGeometryGeoJSON"]) g = g[["shapeName", "geometry"]].rename(columns={"shapeName": "region"}) g["country"], g["iso3"] = c, iso frames.append(g) print(f" {c:15s} {iso}: {len(g)} regions") adm = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True).to_crs("EPSG:4326") adm["region_id"] = adm.iso3 + "_" + adm.groupby("iso3").cumcount().astype(str).str.zfill(3) adm["geometry"] = adm.geometry.make_valid().simplify(0.01, preserve_topology=True) adm[["region_id", "region", "country", "iso3", "geometry"]].to_file(PUBLIC / "admin1.geojson", driver="GeoJSON") print(f"Saved {len(adm)} regions") ``` ::: ## Step 3 · Clustering: k-means profiles and DBSCAN hotspots - **k-means** (`scikit-learn`) on the three *standardized* measures. Choosing k: the elbow plot and the silhouette score both point to **k = 5**. - **DBSCAN** on the latitude/longitude of the "all three high" clusters, with **haversine** (great-circle) distance. Settings: radius 50 km, at least 15 clusters. A sensitivity check covers radii of 25–100 km. ::: {.callout-note collapse=true} ## Show the code: `analysis/04_profiles_hotspots.py` (scikit-learn KMeans, DBSCAN) ```python """Step 4. Cluster profiles (k-means) and spatial hotspots (DBSCAN). * k-means on three standardized measures: anemia, open defecation, malaria. Number of profiles chosen with the elbow method (and silhouette as a check). * DBSCAN on the locations of clusters in the "all three high" profile, using great-circle (haversine) distance, to find spatial hotspots. Input : data/private/clusters_features.parquet Output: data/private/clusters_profiles.parquet (private) data/public/kmeans_elbow.csv, kmeans_profiles.csv, dbscan_summary.csv (public) """ import numpy as np import pandas as pd from sklearn.cluster import KMeans, DBSCAN from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler from config import PRIVATE, PUBLIC K = 5 # elbow bends around 4-5; silhouette is highest at 5 -> 5 profiles EPS_KM, MIN_SAMPLES = 50, 15 MEASURES = ["anemia_pct", "od_pct", "pfpr"] cl = pd.read_parquet(PRIVATE / "clusters_features.parquet") # MAP leaves malaria-free areas (e.g. Lesotho, Eswatini, highlands) blank -> treat as 0 % prevalence cl["pfpr_missing"] = cl.pfpr.isna().astype(int) cl["pfpr"] = cl.pfpr.fillna(0) cl = cl.dropna(subset=MEASURES).reset_index(drop=True) X = StandardScaler().fit_transform(cl[MEASURES]) # ---- elbow ------------------------------------------------------------------ rng = np.random.default_rng(0) sample = rng.choice(len(X), size=min(8000, len(X)), replace=False) rows = [] for k in range(1, 11): km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=10, random_state=0).fit(X) sil = silhouette_score(X[sample], km.labels_[sample]) if k > 1 else np.nan rows.append({"k": k, "inertia": km.inertia_, "silhouette": sil}) elbow = pd.DataFrame(rows) elbow.to_csv(PUBLIC / "kmeans_elbow.csv", index=False) print(elbow.round(3).to_string(index=False)) # ---- final k-means ------------------------------------------------------------ km = KMeans(n_clusters=K, n_init=25, random_state=0).fit(X) cl["profile_raw"] = km.labels_ cent = cl.groupby("profile_raw")[MEASURES].mean() z = (cent - cl[MEASURES].mean()) / cl[MEASURES].std() def name(row): hi = [lbl for lbl, col in [("anemia", "anemia_pct"), ("open defecation", "od_pct"), ("malaria", "pfpr")] if row[col] > 0.25] if len(hi) == 3: return "All three high" if not hi: return "All three low" return "High " + " + ".join(hi) names = z.apply(name, axis=1) # make names unique if two profiles share a label for n, idx in names.groupby(names).groups.items(): if len(idx) > 1: for j, i in enumerate(sorted(idx, key=lambda i: -z.loc[i].sum())): names[i] = f"{n} ({'stronger' if j == 0 else 'weaker'})" order = z.sum(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False).index # 1 = highest burden pid = {raw: i + 1 for i, raw in enumerate(order)} cl["profile"] = cl.profile_raw.map(pid) cl["profile_name"] = cl.profile_raw.map(names) prof = (cl.groupby(["profile", "profile_name"]) .agg(n_clusters=("anemia_pct", "size"), n_children=("n_children", "sum"), anemia_pct=("anemia_pct", "mean"), od_pct=("od_pct", "mean"), pfpr=("pfpr", "mean"), rain_3mo_z=("rain_3mo_z", "mean"), wealth=("wealth", "mean"), mom_secondary_pct=("mom_secondary_pct", "mean"), urban_pct=("urban", "mean")) .reset_index()) prof["urban_pct"] *= 100 prof["share_pct"] = 100 * prof.n_clusters / prof.n_clusters.sum() prof.round(2).to_csv(PUBLIC / "kmeans_profiles.csv", index=False) print(prof.round(1).to_string(index=False)) # ---- DBSCAN hotspots within the highest-burden profile ----------------------- top = cl.profile == 1 coords = np.radians(cl.loc[top, ["lat", "lon"]].to_numpy()) db = DBSCAN(eps=EPS_KM / 6371.0, min_samples=MIN_SAMPLES, metric="haversine", algorithm="ball_tree").fit(coords) cl["hotspot"] = -1 cl.loc[top, "hotspot"] = db.labels_ cl["in_hotspot"] = (cl.hotspot >= 0).astype(int) hs = (cl[cl.hotspot >= 0].groupby("hotspot") .agg(n_clusters=("lat", "size"), countries=("country", lambda s: ", ".join(sorted(s.unique()))), anemia_pct=("anemia_pct", "mean"), od_pct=("od_pct", "mean"), pfpr=("pfpr", "mean")) .sort_values("n_clusters", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)) hs.index = hs.index + 1 hs.index.name = "hotspot" hs.round(1).to_csv(PUBLIC / "dbscan_summary.csv") print(f"\nDBSCAN: {top.sum():,} clusters in profile 1 -> {len(hs)} hotspots, " f"{cl.in_hotspot.sum():,} clusters in a hotspot, {(db.labels_ == -1).sum():,} scattered") print(hs.head(15).round(1).to_string()) # ---- sensitivity: how do hotspots change with the search radius? ------------- sens = [] for eps in (25, 50, 75, 100): lab = DBSCAN(eps=eps / 6371.0, min_samples=MIN_SAMPLES, metric="haversine", algorithm="ball_tree").fit(coords).labels_ cl[f"hot_{eps}"] = 0 cl.loc[top, f"hot_{eps}"] = (lab >= 0).astype(int) sens.append({"eps_km": eps, "n_hotspots": int(lab.max() + 1), "clusters_in_hotspots": int((lab >= 0).sum()), "share_pct": round(100 * (lab >= 0).mean(), 1)}) pd.DataFrame(sens).to_csv(PUBLIC / "dbscan_sensitivity.csv", index=False) print(pd.DataFrame(sens).to_string(index=False)) cl.drop(columns="profile_raw").to_parquet(PRIVATE / "clusters_profiles.parquet", index=False) ``` ::: ## Step 4 · Machine learning: predicting anemia - **Train/test split** of 80/20, **5-fold cross-validation**, and a **grid search** over random forest depth, leaf size, and features per split. - A **linear regression** pipeline (`StandardScaler` → `LinearRegression`) as the baseline. - **Spatial lag:** the average anemia of the 10 nearest *training* clusters, found with a `BallTree` and haversine distance. Test clusters only "see" training neighbours, so no answers leak in. - **Permutation importance** shows which features matter. **Out-of-fold predictions** give every cluster a prediction from a model that never saw it, which feeds the error map. ::: {.callout-note collapse=true} ## Show the code: `analysis/05_predict_anemia.py` (scikit-learn) ```python """Step 5. Predict cluster anemia prevalence: linear regression vs random forest. * Features: open defecation, malaria, rainfall anomaly, long-term rainfall, wealth, maternal education, urban, and a spatial lag (average anemia of the 10 nearest *training* clusters, so the test set never leaks into features). * 80/20 train/test split, 5-fold cross-validation, grid search for the forest. * Out-of-fold predictions for every cluster -> where does the model miss? Input : data/private/clusters_profiles.parquet Output: data/private/clusters_final.parquet (private) data/public/model_scores.csv, feature_importance.csv (public) """ import numpy as np import pandas as pd from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, r2_score from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, KFold, train_test_split from sklearn.neighbors import BallTree from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler from config import PRIVATE, PUBLIC BASE_FEATURES = ["od_pct", "pfpr", "rain_3mo_z", "rain_annual_mm", "wealth", "mom_secondary_pct", "urban"] LABELS = {"od_pct": "Open defecation (%)", "pfpr": "Malaria prevalence (%)", "rain_3mo_z": "Rainfall anomaly, last 3 months", "rain_annual_mm": "Typical annual rainfall", "wealth": "Household wealth", "mom_secondary_pct": "Mothers with secondary school (%)", "urban": "Urban", "spatial_lag": "Anemia in nearby clusters"} K_NEIGHBORS = 10 y_col = "anemia_pct" cl = pd.read_parquet(PRIVATE / "clusters_profiles.parquet") cl = cl.dropna(subset=BASE_FEATURES + [y_col]).reset_index(drop=True) print(f"{len(cl):,} clusters with complete features") def spatial_lag(train_idx, target_idx, k=K_NEIGHBORS): """Mean anemia of the k nearest training clusters (excluding the cluster itself).""" tr = cl.loc[train_idx] tree = BallTree(np.radians(tr[["lat", "lon"]].to_numpy()), metric="haversine") dist, ind = tree.query(np.radians(cl.loc[target_idx, ["lat", "lon"]].to_numpy()), k=k + 1) tr_ids = tr.index.to_numpy()[ind] # (n, k+1) training-cluster ids vals = tr[y_col].to_numpy()[ind] self_hit = tr_ids == np.asarray(target_idx)[:, None] vals = np.where(self_hit, np.nan, vals) # keep the first k non-self neighbours return np.array([row[~np.isnan(row)][:k].mean() for row in vals]) FEATURES = BASE_FEATURES + ["spatial_lag"] def make_xy(train_idx, test_idx): Xtr = cl.loc[train_idx, BASE_FEATURES].copy(); Xtr["spatial_lag"] = spatial_lag(train_idx, train_idx) Xte = cl.loc[test_idx, BASE_FEATURES].copy(); Xte["spatial_lag"] = spatial_lag(train_idx, test_idx) return Xtr, cl.loc[train_idx, y_col], Xte, cl.loc[test_idx, y_col] train_idx, test_idx = train_test_split(cl.index, test_size=0.2, random_state=42) Xtr, ytr, Xte, yte = make_xy(train_idx, test_idx) cv = KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=0) grid = GridSearchCV( RandomForestRegressor(random_state=0, n_jobs=-1), {"n_estimators": [300], "max_depth": [10, 20, None], "min_samples_leaf": [5, 20], "max_features": [0.33, 0.66]}, cv=cv, scoring="r2", n_jobs=1) def cv_r2(make_model, feats): """Average R2 across the 5 cross-validation folds of the training set.""" return np.mean([r2_score(ytr.iloc[v], make_model().fit(Xtr[feats].iloc[t], ytr.iloc[t]) .predict(Xtr[feats].iloc[v])) for t, v in cv.split(Xtr)]) grid.fit(Xtr[FEATURES], ytr) # grid search with 5-fold CV best = {k: v for k, v in grid.best_params_.items()} make_linear = lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LinearRegression()) make_rf = lambda: RandomForestRegressor(random_state=0, n_jobs=-1, **best) rows = [] for name, make_model, feats in [("Linear regression", make_linear, FEATURES), ("Random forest", make_rf, FEATURES), ("Random forest (no spatial lag)", make_rf, BASE_FEATURES)]: model = make_model().fit(Xtr[feats], ytr) pred = model.predict(Xte[feats]) rows.append({"model": name, "cv_r2": cv_r2(make_model, feats), "test_r2": r2_score(yte, pred), "test_mae": mean_absolute_error(yte, pred)}) print(rows[-1]) if name == "Linear regression": linear = model print("Best forest:", grid.best_params_) scores = pd.DataFrame(rows) scores.round(3).to_csv(PUBLIC / "model_scores.csv", index=False) # ---- which factors matter? (permutation importance on the test set) --------- rf = grid.best_estimator_ imp = permutation_importance(rf, Xte[FEATURES], yte, n_repeats=10, random_state=0, n_jobs=-1) lin_coef = linear.named_steps["linearregression"].coef_ fi = pd.DataFrame({"feature": FEATURES, "label": [LABELS[f] for f in FEATURES], "rf_importance": imp.importances_mean, "rf_importance_sd": imp.importances_std, "linear_std_coef": lin_coef}) fi.sort_values("rf_importance", ascending=False).round(4).to_csv(PUBLIC / "feature_importance.csv", index=False) print(fi.sort_values("rf_importance", ascending=False).round(3).to_string(index=False)) # ---- out-of-fold predictions for every cluster (for the error map) ---------- cl["pred_rf"] = np.nan cl["pred_linear"] = np.nan for t, v in KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=1).split(cl): Xa, ya, Xb, _ = make_xy(cl.index[t], cl.index[v]) cl.loc[cl.index[v], "pred_rf"] = make_rf().fit(Xa, ya).predict(Xb) cl.loc[cl.index[v], "pred_linear"] = make_linear().fit(Xa, ya).predict(Xb) cl["resid_rf"] = cl[y_col] - cl.pred_rf # + = model under-predicts anemia cl["abs_err_rf"] = cl.resid_rf.abs() print("Out-of-fold R2 (rf / linear):", round(r2_score(cl[y_col], cl.pred_rf), 3), round(r2_score(cl[y_col], cl.pred_linear), 3)) cl.to_parquet(PRIVATE / "clusters_final.parquet", index=False) ``` ::: ## Step 5 · Privacy-safe aggregation and the website ::: {.privacy} **DHS rules do not allow publishing cluster GPS points or microdata.** The raw DHS data and every cluster-level file stay on my computer. They are excluded by `.gitignore` and never pushed to GitHub. Everything on this site is aggregated: - **Hexagons** (H3 resolution 4, ~23 km edge, ~1,770 km²), shown only if they hold **at least 3 clusters**. The real H3 cell ids are dropped. - **Admin-1 regions**, shown only with **at least 5 clusters**. - **Malaria and rainfall rasters** are open data and are shown in full. ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse=true} ## Show the code: `analysis/06_public_outputs.py` (h3, geopandas) ```python """Step 6. Aggregate private cluster results into PUBLIC, non-identifying outputs. DHS forbids sharing cluster GPS points, so everything published is aggregated: * hexagons (H3 resolution 4, ~23 km edge, ~1,770 km2), hidden if < 3 clusters * admin-1 regions, hidden if < 5 clusters * open raster layers (MAP malaria, CHIRPS rainfall) as map images Output (data/public/): hexes.geojson, regions.geojson, profiles_by_country.csv, raster_*.png + raster_bounds.json, sample_summary.json """ import json import h3 import numpy as np import pandas as pd import geopandas as gpd import rasterio import xarray as xr import matplotlib import matplotlib.image from matplotlib import cm, colors from shapely.geometry import Polygon from config import PRIVATE, PUBLIC, MAP_DIR, CHIRPS_MONTHLY, AFRICA_BBOX H3_RES, MIN_HEX, MIN_REGION = 4, 3, 5 cl = pd.read_parquet(PRIVATE / "clusters_final.parquet") allc = pd.read_parquet(PRIVATE / "clusters_profiles.parquet") # includes clusters w/o all model features allc = allc.merge(cl[["idhspsu", "pred_rf", "resid_rf", "abs_err_rf"]], on="idhspsu", how="left") n_prof = allc.profile.max() def summarise(g): out = g.agg(n_clusters=("idhspsu", "size"), n_children=("n_children", "sum"), anemia_pct=("anemia_pct", "mean"), modsev_anemia_pct=("modsev_anemia_pct", "mean"), od_pct=("od_pct", "mean"), pfpr=("pfpr", "mean"), rain_3mo_z=("rain_3mo_z", "mean"), rain_annual_mm=("rain_annual_mm", "mean"), wealth=("wealth", "mean"), mom_secondary_pct=("mom_secondary_pct", "mean"), urban_pct=("urban", "mean"), in_hotspot_pct=("in_hotspot", "mean"), pred_anemia_pct=("pred_rf", "mean"), resid=("resid_rf", "mean"), abs_err=("abs_err_rf", "mean"), year_min=("int_year", "min"), year_max=("int_year", "max"), hot_25=("hot_25", "mean"), hot_50=("hot_50", "mean"), hot_75=("hot_75", "mean"), hot_100=("hot_100", "mean"), country=("country", lambda s: s.mode().iat[0])) for e in (25, 50, 75, 100): out[f"hot_{e}"] *= 100 out["urban_pct"] *= 100 out["in_hotspot_pct"] *= 100 shares = pd.crosstab(g.obj[g.keys] if isinstance(g.keys, str) else g.obj[g.keys[0]], g.obj["profile"], normalize="index") * 100 shares = shares.reindex(columns=range(1, n_prof + 1), fill_value=0) shares.columns = [f"profile{p}_pct" for p in shares.columns] out = out.join(shares) out["profile"] = shares.to_numpy().argmax(axis=1) + 1 # most common profile names = allc.drop_duplicates("profile").set_index("profile").profile_name out["profile_name"] = out.profile.map(names) # dominant DBSCAN hotspot id (0 = none) hs = g.obj[g.obj.hotspot >= 0].groupby(g.keys).hotspot.agg(lambda s: s.mode().iat[0] + 1) out["hotspot_id"] = hs.reindex(out.index).fillna(0).astype(int) return out # ---- hexagons ------------------------------------------------------------------ allc["hex"] = [h3.latlng_to_cell(la, lo, H3_RES) for la, lo in zip(allc.lat, allc.lon)] hx = summarise(allc.groupby("hex")) hx = hx[hx.n_clusters >= MIN_HEX].reset_index() hx["geometry"] = [Polygon([(lo, la) for la, lo in h3.cell_to_boundary(h)]) for h in hx.hex] hx = gpd.GeoDataFrame(hx, crs="EPSG:4326").round(2) hx["hex"] = range(1, len(hx) + 1) # drop the real H3 id hx.to_file(PUBLIC / "hexes.geojson", driver="GeoJSON") print(f"Hexes: {len(hx):,} shown (>= {MIN_HEX} clusters), covering {hx.n_clusters.sum():,} of {len(allc):,} clusters") # ---- admin-1 regions ----------------------------------------------------------- adm = gpd.read_file(PUBLIC / "admin1.geojson") pts = gpd.GeoDataFrame(allc, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(allc.lon, allc.lat), crs="EPSG:4326") pts = gpd.sjoin(pts, adm[["region_id", "geometry"]], how="left", predicate="within") # clusters falling just outside a polygon (coast, displacement) -> nearest region miss = pts.region_id.isna() if miss.any(): near = gpd.sjoin_nearest(pts.loc[miss, ["geometry"]].to_crs(3857), adm[["region_id", "geometry"]].to_crs(3857), how="left") pts.loc[miss, "region_id"] = near.groupby(level=0).region_id.first() pts = pd.DataFrame(pts.drop(columns=["geometry", "index_right"])) rg = summarise(pts.groupby("region_id")).drop(columns="country") rg = rg[rg.n_clusters >= MIN_REGION] regions = adm.merge(rg.reset_index(), on="region_id", how="left").round(2) regions.to_file(PUBLIC / "regions.geojson", driver="GeoJSON") print(f"Regions: {rg.shape[0]} of {len(adm)} with >= {MIN_REGION} clusters") # ---- by country ------------------------------------------------------------------ bc = (pd.crosstab(allc.country, allc.profile_name, normalize="index") * 100).round(1) bc["n_clusters"] = allc.groupby("country").size() bc["anemia_pct"] = allc.groupby("country").anemia_pct.mean().round(1) bc.reset_index().to_csv(PUBLIC / "profiles_by_country.csv", index=False) # ---- open raster layers as images (for map overlays) ----------------------------- def to_png(arr, path, cmap, vmin, vmax): rgba = matplotlib.colormaps[cmap](colors.Normalize(vmin, vmax)(arr)) rgba[..., 3] = np.where(np.isnan(arr), 0, 0.75) matplotlib.image.imsave(path, rgba) bounds = {} for yr in (2005, 2020): with rasterio.open(MAP_DIR / f"PfPR_2-10_Africa_{yr}.tif") as src: a = src.read(1).astype("float32") a[a < 0] = np.nan a = a[::2, ::2] * 100 # ~10 km, enough for a web map to_png(a, PUBLIC / f"raster_malaria_{yr}.png", "YlOrRd", 0, 70) b = src.bounds bounds[f"malaria_{yr}"] = [[b.bottom, b.left], [b.top, b.right]] lon0, lat0, lon1, lat1 = AFRICA_BBOX ann = [] for y in range(1981, 2011): da = xr.open_dataset(CHIRPS_MONTHLY / f"CHIRPS_monthly_{y}.nc")["precip"] ann.append(da.sel(longitude=slice(lon0, lon1), latitude=slice(lat1, lat0))[:, ::4, ::4].sum("time").values) ann = np.mean(ann, axis=0) ann[ann <= 0] = np.nan to_png(ann, PUBLIC / "raster_rain_annual.png", "YlGnBu", 0, 2500) bounds["rain_annual"] = [[lat0, lon0], [lat1, lon1]] json.dump(bounds, open(PUBLIC / "raster_bounds.json", "w")) # ---- headline numbers ------------------------------------------------------------ flow = pd.read_csv(PRIVATE / "sample_flow.csv") summary = {"children": int(allc.n_children.sum()), "clusters": len(allc), "countries": int(allc.country.nunique()), "surveys": int(allc["sample"].nunique()), "year_min": int(allc.int_year.min()), "year_max": int(allc.int_year.max()), "anemia_pct": round(float(allc.anemia_pct.mean()), 1), "hex_shown": len(hx), "regions_shown": int(rg.shape[0]), "sample_flow": flow.to_dict(orient="records")} json.dump(summary, open(PUBLIC / "sample_summary.json", "w"), indent=2) print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in summary.items() if k != "sample_flow"})) ``` ::: **Visualization tools:** `folium` for the Leaflet maps (layer control, a custom measure picker, synced dual maps, raster image overlays) and `Altair` for the linked charts (brushing, click-to-filter, legend selection, sliders, drop-downs). The site is built with Quarto and hosted on GitHub Pages. ## Reproducing this ```bash python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/activate pip install -r requirements.txt cd analysis python 01_build_clusters.py # needs your own DHS extract (see README) python 02_raster_features.py # needs MAP + CHIRPS rasters python 03_download_boundaries.py python 04_profiles_hotspots.py python 05_predict_anemia.py python 06_public_outputs.py cd .. && quarto render ``` ## Limitations - **Cross-sectional data:** this is about association and prediction, not cause and effect. - **Surveys from different years are pooled** (2000–2021). A hexagon can mix surveys taken 15 years apart. - **Malaria is modelled, not measured** in the cluster. MAP surfaces are themselves smoothed predictions. - **Small samples:** many clusters have 5–15 tested children, so cluster anemia rates are noisy. This limits how well any model can do. - **GPS displacement** blurs the raster extraction, which the buffers only partly fix. - **Country coverage:** only surveys that tested children's hemoglobin *and* released GPS are included. In this extract, DR Congo and Côte d'Ivoire have no GPS, Zambia and Chad have no anemia classification, and Kenya has too few tested children with complete data. All five drop out.
